Spencer Hawes is an American basketball player.  He is the nephew of [[Steve Hawes]], the retired NBA player.

==High school==
Hawes played [[Center (basketball)|center]] at [[Seattle Prep]], where he led his team to win the state championship for the 2005-2006 season and was named the tournament MVP. He might have entered the [[2006 NBA Draft]] had the NBA not enacted a new rule requiring players to wait a year after their class graduates from high school.  He and [[Martell Webster]] were teammates at Seattle Preparatory School.

*Following the 2005-2006 season, Hawes was selected as an [[Associated Press]] [[All-American]], [[McDonald's All-American]], [[Parade Magazine]] All-American, and [[USA Today]] All-American[http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/basketball/2006-04-17-boys-all-usa-team_x.htm].

*Named 2006 [[Gatorade]] Boys Basketball Washington Player of the Year and [[Seattle Times]] player of the year.

*In the summer of 2006, he played for the [[USA Basketball]] Under-18 team (coached by Washington's [[Lorenzo Romar]]) which defeated Argentina to win the gold medal at the [[FIBA]] Americas Under-18 Championship. In the final game, he scored 24 points and had 10 rebounds.

==College==
Coach Romar has said he expects Hawes to play a major role for the Washington team during his freshman year, with plenty of minutes available after the departure of four seniors from the 2005-2006 team, including NBA guards [[Brandon Roy]] ([[Portland Trail Blazers]]) and [[Bobby Jones (Washington Huskies)|Bobby Jones]] ([[Philadelphia 76ers]]). NBA draft projection services say he will be a lottery pick when he goes pro, which could be as soon as 2007, following his freshman year.[http://draftexpress.com/mock.php?y=2007]

==NBA Draft==
Spencer Hawes has announced he will declare for the 2007 NBA Draft, but has not hired an agent.

He is considered a draft project due to his low upper and lower body strength. Though his advanced offensive game will still likely keep him a lottery pick.
